name: Sportradar Group AG (Nasdaq: SRAD)
analyst_actions: 2026-08-17 | Weiss Ratings | Upgrade | Hold C- -> Hold C
2026-08-10 | Bank of America Securities | Maintains | Buy
upcoming_dates: 2026-11-04 | earnings | Q3 2026 results date, estimated and not company-confirmed | https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/srad/statistics/ | aggregator
product: Sportradar sells sports data, live odds, streaming and audiovisual rights, betting platform and managed trading services, integrity services, marketing and affiliate services, and a newer iGaming product called Playradar.
demand: Demand is broad and growing for premium content, streaming and odds, with prediction markets the newest source; US growth is moderating with no significant new state openings while rest-of-world grows about 20%.
pricing_power: Pricing power looks moderate but improving; the company leans on exclusive premium rights and cross-sell rather than headline price increases, and content growth is volume and mix led.
competition: The main competitor is Genius Sports, alongside rival data, odds and trading suppliers; Sportradar differentiates on scale of over one million events a year, exclusive rights and integrity services, and now competes indirectly with in-house league data efforts.
team: CEO Carsten Koerl and CFO Craig Felenstein lead; the company is running a cost-efficiency and AI-driven automation program with restructuring and severance costs, and employs about 4,882 people.
market_strategy: Strategy is to monetize exclusive rights, notably IMG ARENA, upsell and cross-sell into a global client base, and expand into prediction markets and iGaming while cutting costs and returning capital through a $1bn buyback.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue rose 19% to EUR 378m on 27% content growth, Kalshi and Polymarket deals expand prediction markets, and management guides FY2026 revenue EUR 1,518-1,533m with FCF conversion above 56%.
bear: FY2026 guidance was cut on delayed prediction-market and moderating US growth; Q2 missed estimates, EPS -$0.01, UBS and BTIG downgraded, rights costs rose 30%, and a Rosen class action alleges weak KYC.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-04 showing FY2026 revenue guidance below EUR 1,518m or Adjusted EBITDA margin contraction would prove the bull case wrong.
web_what_changed: On 2026-08-03 Sportradar reported Q2 2026 revenue up 19% to EUR 378m but cut FY2026 guidance, citing delayed prediction-market deals and moderating US growth; UBS and BTIG downgraded the stock, the company signed Kalshi and expanded its Polymarket prediction-market deals, and repurchased about $140m of shares in the quarter.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company disclosure dated 2026-09-24 was located; the last dated items were analyst notes on 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22, when the stock rose about 7.5%.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix, not price. Growth came from Betting and Gaming Content up 27% on IMG ARENA cross-sell and new customer uptake, plus managed turnover of about $56bn trailing twelve months, up 26%, while Managed Betting Services revenue was flat year over year.
web_suppliers: Key suppliers are sports rights owners including the ATP, NBA, NHL, MLB, MLS, PGA TOUR, UEFA, FIFA, Bundesliga, Wimbledon (AELTC) and Euroleague. Rights are locked long-term, but sports rights expense rose 30% to EUR 138m and cloud costs rose, so cost, not availability, is the constraint.
web_customers: Named clients include Flutter, DraftKings, Google, Microsoft, Kalshi, Polymarket and Novig, plus sportsbooks and media companies. Exact concentration is not disclosed, but a small number of large operators and US clients, at 27% of revenue, dominate.
web_who_loses: Rival data, odds and trading suppliers such as Genius Sports lose share, and traditional sportsbooks lose handle if prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket keep growing. Leagues that build in-house data or sell direct would also displace Sportradar.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue of about $431m missed the $436m estimate and EPS of -$0.01 missed by $0.08; FY2026 guidance was cut; UBS and BTIG downgraded; the stock is down about 56% over 52 weeks; and a Rosen securities class action alleges Sportradar worked with black-market gambling operators with weak KYC (Class Period 2024-11-07 to 2026-04-21).
web_if_management_right: Prediction markets and iGaming expand the addressable market, prediction-market revenue accelerates in H2 2026, FY2026 revenue reaches EUR 1,518 to 1,533m and Adjusted EBITDA EUR 360 to 368m, with continued margin expansion and free cash flow conversion above the 2025 level of 56%.
web_if_management_wrong: Prediction-market and US growth stay delayed while sports rights and cloud costs keep rising and FX keeps hurting reported earnings; the first thing to break is Adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow conversion, which undercuts the buyback thesis.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Cloud and infrastructure providers such as Microsoft Azure and AWS, rights-owning leagues and clubs including the ATP, Bundesliga, Euroleague and Wimbledon, prediction-market brokers and market makers, and affiliate and marketing partners.
